data.body_html:
When planning a luxury yacht charter, two destinations often come to mind: Marbella and Cannes. Both offer glamour, sun, and sea, but which one gives you the best experience for your money? This Marbella yacht charter vs Cannes comparison breaks down costs, boats, weather, and exclusivity so you can decide with confidence.

Cost Comparison: Marbella vs Cannes

Cost is a major factor. In Marbella, a 2-hour charter on an Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) costs €749 all-inclusive: skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and 21% IVA. The same duration in Cannes on a comparable boat starts around €1,200, with fuel (€300–€600) and VAT (20%) often added separately. For a full day, Marbella offers the Azimut 39 (11 pax) at €2,299 for 8 hours. In Cannes, expect €3,500+ before extras. The savings are clear.

Fleet and Boat Quality

Our fleet in Marbella includes 16+ boats, from the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) to the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). All depart from Puerto Banús. Cannes has many charter companies but often with older models or smaller boats at the same price. For example, a Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) in Marbella costs €4,719 for 4 hours, including a free jet ski. In Cannes, a similar vessel would be €6,000+ without the jet ski. Compare our yacht charter Marbella options to see the range.

Weather and Sailing Conditions

Marbella boasts over 300 sunny days per year, with summer temperatures averaging 30°C and calm seas. Cannes has around 230 sunny days and can be windier, especially in spring and autumn. The Mediterranean coast near Marbella offers sheltered anchorages like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, perfect for swimming and relaxation. Cannes has the Lérins Islands, but they can get crowded during peak season.

Exclusivity and Anchorages

Marbella offers hidden gems like Cabopino and Río Verde within 30 minutes of Puerto Banús. These coves are less frequented than Cannes hotspots like Île Sainte-Marguerite. For a truly exclusive experience, head to Estepona or Sotogrande. Cannes is more built up, with the Croisette and Film Festival glamour, but the anchorages are more public and busy. Marbella's coastline gives you space to enjoy the sea without the crowds.

Inclusions and Hidden Costs

Every Marbella charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. In Cannes, many charters exclude fuel (€300–€600 extra), crew gratuity (10–15%), and sometimes even water. Our transparent pricing means you know the total upfront. For example, the Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) is available on request with full inclusions – no surprises.

Nightlife and Vibe

Puerto Banús is the epicentre of Marbella's nightlife, with beach clubs like Ocean Club and Pangea offering VIP tables and DJ sets. Cannes has the Croisette and Festival glamour but is more formal and expensive. Marbella is relaxed, party-oriented, and welcoming to all. Whether you want a quiet sunset cruise or a lively evening, Marbella delivers.

Which Destination Wins?

If you value value for money, sunshine, and exclusive anchorages, Marbella is the clear winner. Cannes has its charm, but the hidden costs and crowded waters make it less appealing for the savvy traveller. For a yacht charter Marbella experience that combines luxury and affordability, start your journey with us.
